newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer, CVG say court didn't weaken tenure.
newsitem.headline: Placer, CVG say court didn't weaken tenure.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc and its Venezuelan joint venture partner Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG) reiterated Monday that their rights over the Las Cristinas gold deposit in Venezuela are secure.

Crystallex International Corp earlier said it acquired rights to two blocks of the property by buying a Venezualan company "whose ownership rights have been confirmed by final and binding decisions" of Venezuela's Supreme Court.
But Placer said the Supreme Court decisions "do not deal with the substantive question of title... To the contrary these decisions deal solely with technical procedural issues."
Those issues related "to interim assignments of prior concessions made in 1987," Placer said.

One of the original concessions covering Las Cristinas that was involved in the Supreme Court decision "effectively expired in 1989 and the other was declared revoked by the Ministry of Energy and Mines in the same year," Placer said.
In 1991, the rights to Las Cristinas were granted to CVG, which struck a joint venture with Placer in 1992. Placer holds 70 percent and CVG the rest.

"Because the facts that occurred subsequent to 1987 were not relevant to its decision and because the substantive issue of title to the concessions was not being litigated, those facts were not before the Supreme Court," Placer said.
Thus the Supreme Court decisions on which Crystallex based its claims "are wholly irrelevant to the right of tenure of CVG. Hence the rights...are secure and valid in law."
Neither Placer nor CVG are in any discussions over ownership of the project.
